verses.1: And Deborah and Barak, son of Abiram, stood up that day, as it was said.
verses.2: In Pharaoh’s time, the kings of Israel were kind to their people. Jehovah blessed them.
verses.3: Hear, kings! Listen carefully. I, the servant of the LORD, will say these words to the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.4: YHWH, as you departed from Sheol, in your steps from the field of Adam. The land was filled with noise; even the skies were shattered. Even the giants were destroyed by the waters.
verses.5: The mountains trembled before Jehovah; Sina’i trembled before Jehovah, the God of Israel.
verses.6: In the days of Shmaggar ben-Anat, and in the days of Ya’el, people stopped traveling on foot. Those who used to walk along the paths now walked on horseback.
verses.7: They stopped their destruction in Israel. They stopped until I could rebuild it again. I rebuilt it, even though it was still in Israel.
verses.8: God will choose new ones as bread for the doors; they will be a protection against those who see and destroy them. This will happen in Israel, where there are four thousand people.
verses.9: My heart grieves for Israel, which is being destroyed by the enemy. May Jehovah bless them.
verses.10: Those who ride on the backs of dragons, those who sit on thrones, and those who walk along the paths of darkness.
verses.11: From the sound of trumpets, people would come from everywhere. There, Jehovah would give them justice and righteousness. Then they would go down to the gates, along with the people of Jehovah.
verses.12: Oh, my Lord! Oh, my Lord! My words are like songs. May the light rise again, and may He who created me return to you, Son of Avraham.
verses.13: Then the remnant of the people of Jehovah descended among the nobles. They came down to the rulers.
verses.14: From me, Ephraim, whose roots lie in Amalek. After you, in your own land. From me, I know that they will descend from Hakkim and Zebulun, and they will be seated in the throne of the writer.
verses.15: And the singers in Issachar shall sing with their voices. They will also sing beautifully, as if they were singing in the depths of the wilderness, where their feet tread on the steps of great heights.
verses.16: Why do you sit among the mountains, to hear the sounds of the wild animals and the cries of the great birds? You are a seeker of the heart.
verses.17: Gilad lived across the Jordan River. He wondered why those who lived on the shore of the sea would have to live in such a difficult situation.
verses.18: Zevulun, with a perverse heart, will perish and be destroyed on the mountains of destruction.
verses.19: Kings came and fought. Then, the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach. They fought over the gold coins that were given as gifts; they didn’t take them.
verses.20: From heaven, the stars fought against each other. They fought with Sisra.
verses.21: Nahal Kishon G’rafam, Nahal Kedumim, Nahal Kishon Tidrki, Nafshi Ozz.
verses.22: Then the riders followed their horses from one place to another.
verses.23: Let them be destroyed! The Lord has said, “Let their houses be destroyed!” For they did not come to help the Lord. They did not come to help the Lord in times of crisis.
verses.24: May she be blessed by women. May the wife of my friend be blessed by women in the tent of blessing.
verses.25: Water was given as milk, in magnificent vessels. It was offered with heat.
verses.26: Her right hand will be sent forth to help those who are burdened and tired. Her left hand will also be used to help them. She will remove their burdens and ease their suffering.
verses.27: Between her legs, she fell down. She lay there, broken and defeated. In the place where she fell, a dead body lay.
verses.28: In the midst of the flames, Isra’s mother stood up and tried to get out of the burning carriage. She tried to get away from the flames, but her carriage kept burning further and further.
verses.29: Her wise words will answer her. Even then, they will still be heard by her.
verses.30: They will not find any sharers in their generosity and compassion. They will give nothing but mercy and compassion to those who are worthy of it. They will mend the wounds of those who are injured.
verses.31: So all your enemies will be destroyed, LORD, and your followers too. Just as the sun sets in its glory, so too will the earth be calm for forty years.
